stations.name: Edmonton area
stations.notes: Parkland; frost pockets in low spots; good for hardy fruits with wind protection.

stations.name: Calgary area
stations.notes: Chinooks, wind, and variable snowpack. Shelterbelts and microclimates are critical.

stations.name: Red Deer area
stations.notes: Central parkland transition; solid homestead climate with wind exposure on open quarters.

stations.name: Lethbridge area
stations.notes: Semi-arid; irrigation or serious water harvesting; chinook-influenced winters.

stations.name: Medicine Hat area
stations.notes: One of Alberta's warmest, driest zones. Drought design first.

stations.name: Grande Prairie area
stations.notes: Peace Country: long days, short season; prioritize early cultivars and season extension.

stations.name: Fort McMurray area
stations.notes: Boreal transition; focus on hardiest species and thermal mass / shelter.

stations.name: Peace River area
stations.notes: Short season agriculture belt; water and wind design matter.

stations.name: Brooks / SE Alberta
stations.notes: Irrigation country; soil building and water efficiency dominate design.

stations.name: Rocky Mountain House area
stations.notes: Cooler foothills moisture; good for trees, shorter for heat-loving crops.

disclaimer: Approximate climate normals for design guidance only — not a substitute for local station data or professional engineering. Values are generalized for permaculture planning across Alberta regions.
